acceptance_criteria.criterion: add({ url: 'https://token@github.com/org/repo.git' }) stores the URL as 'https://github.com/org/repo.git'.
A console.warn is emitted when credentials are stripped.
The duplicate-URL check compares against the clean URL, not the original.
Adding a URL without embedded credentials is unaffected.
Unit tests cover both the stripping path and the clean-URL path.

summary: In `RepositoryManager.add()`, strip embedded credentials from `params.url` before storing; emit `console.warn` instructing users to use `gitCredentials` in config.json.
Duplicate-URL check now compares against `cleanUrl`, not `params.url`, so a token-bearing URL matches an existing clean-URL entry.
Updated existing redaction test to no longer assert `***@` in error: credentials are stripped before the check so the clean URL is what appears in errors.
Added 4 new tests: credential stripping, warn emission, duplicate comparison, and no-op for clean URLs.
Build clean (tsc). All 34 repository manager tests pass.

comments.note: The existing test 'add does not expose credentials in duplicate URL error messages' checked for `***@` in the error message. After credential stripping, the clean URL is stored and used for duplicate checks, so the error message no longer contains `***@` — the assertion was updated to only verify that the raw token is absent. This is the correct security guarantee.

The `console.warn` call in `RepositoryManager.add()` is the only production use of `console.warn` in the codebase. If a structured logger is introduced in future, this should be migrated. Not an issue now.

comments.note: INFO — A02: Credential-stripping logic in RepositoryManager.add() is clean. hasEmbeddedCredentials() gate prevents unnecessary stripEmbeddedCredentials() calls on clean URLs. cleanUrl is consistently used for both duplicate-URL comparison and storage. redactUrl() is correctly applied to error messages before the stripping step runs (to handle errors thrown from slug inference), and applied to cleanUrl in the post-strip duplicate error (where no credentials remain — a no-op, correct). No credential exposure path identified in any throw branch.

INFO — Code structure: inferSlugFromUrl(params.url) processes the raw credential-bearing URL, but only to extract the URL path component (slug). No logging or storage occurs inside inferSlugFromUrl. Performing stripping before slug inference would be marginally more defensive but would require re-engineering the ID inference flow. Not a security issue under current implementation.

[documentation-forward] repository.manager.ts contains two credential-handling utilities side by side: the private redactUrl() helper (regex-based, for error message interpolation) and the imported stripEmbeddedCredentials() (WHATWG URL object + regex fallback, for clean URL production). Their distinct purposes are not immediately obvious to contributors. A brief inline comment on redactUrl() clarifying 'used only for error message interpolation — not for production URL sanitisation' would prevent a future developer from incorrectly unifying them.

Test for console.warn correctly uses try/finally to restore the original console.warn reference regardless of test outcome — good test hygiene. Pattern is consistent with the project's test conventions.
No other observations — implementation scope is narrow and correct. All credential paths correctly flow through cleanUrl before any persistence or comparison operation.
